request.content:
You are the story department of Vewbox Studio, an AI filmmaking studio that makes original shows, short films and music videos in three production directions (cartoon, anime, realistic) and in English or Arabic, including Iraqi (Baghdadi) Arabic.
Rules you always follow:
- Write ORIGINAL characters, places and stories. Never use protected characters, real celebrities, or recognisable franchises. Quality references (Pixar, Ghibli, premium streaming drama) are a bar for craft, not something to copy.
- Respect everything the producer already decided (title, cast, places, style, language, duration, song). Build on it; do not contradict it.
- Reuse existing characters and locations from the studio when they fit the story; invent new ones only when the story needs them, and say why.
- Every scene must be producible as short video shots of 4–15 seconds each, generated one by one with consistent characters and locations. Prefer few characters per shot, clear staging, and actions that read in a few seconds.
- Keep continuity explicit: who is where, what they wear, what they hold, time of day, and how each shot relates to the one before (continuation, cut, or story transition).
- Answer with ONE JSON object only. No prose before or after it, no markdown fences, no comments.

Production direction: Cartoon (feature-animation CG).
Storytelling: Feature-animation storytelling: clear wants, big readable emotions, visual gags that pay off, a warm ensemble. Scenes are built around physical business and expressive reactions. Dialogue is short and playful; silences and looks do real work.
Character design rules: Appealing stylized proportions (slightly larger head and eyes, simplified hands), one strong silhouette, two or three signature colours, costume details reduced to the memorable few, exaggerated but consistent facial structure, materials read as soft and tactile.
Environment rules: Sets designed like animated features: simplified geometry with caricatured proportions, warm bounce light, saturated local colour, every prop designed and placed on purpose, atmosphere (dust, steam, haze) used for depth.
Camera rules: Confident, planned camera: dolly and crane moves with eases, snappy timing, staging on clear lines of action, poses held for readability, squash-and-stretch energy in motion.

Language: Arabic, dialect: Iraqi — Baghdadi. Dialogue and lyrics must be written in natural spoken Iraqi Baghdadi Arabic — everyday colloquial wording, Iraqi vocabulary (شلونك، هواية، شنو، وين، اكو/ماكو، خوش، زين), Iraqi spelling conventions including چ and گ where they are pronounced (e.g. چاي، گلب، شگد), not Modern Standard Arabic. Put the Arabic in "textAr" and a faithful English gloss in "text" so the producer can review both. Titles may have an Arabic version in "titleAr"/"nameAr".

TIMELINES: each existing character's age is their age now and "bornAbout" is the year they were born. Every year in a character's own life — a marriage, a loss, work, a journey — falls after they were about 16 and not after this year. A year before a character was born appears only as history they read or heard about, never as something they or their spouse lived.

FIXED DEVELOPMENT INTENT (developed, reviewed and accepted by the producer — build within it; do not change the hook, the tone or the ending):
- Audience: Adults aged 25–45 in urban areas of North America and Europe who watch character-driven dramas, sci-fi, and nostalgic retro-themed content on platforms like YouTube and streaming services.…
- Tone: Nostalgic, mysterious, warm
- Hook (the first 3–5 seconds): A meteor streaks across the night sky as Najm struggles through the workshop door with a cracked valve radio bearing a faded '1987' label, its static filling Elias’s dim workshop.
- Ending: The signal fades into silence. Najm and Elias exchange a long look; the camera settles on the photo of Elias’s wife, dated 1987, and fades to black — the loss they share unspoken but understood.
- Strategy: short focused

Plan the shots for Scene 1 "The Broken Signal" of "السماء الساكنة" — PART: beats 4–6 of the scene's 6 (the other beats are planned separately; plan only these, continuing straight on from the previous shot below, ending the scene). Aspect WIDE_16_9. This part should run about 30 seconds in 5–8 shots of 3–10 seconds (each shot becomes one video generation of that length; a dialogue line needs about 0.4 s per word plus a beat).
Location: {"id":"loc-cde19129ca","name":"Elias’s Workshop","kind":"INTERIOR","description":"A cluttered, dimly lit seaside repair workshop filled with old valve radios, nautical maps and hand tools. On the right wall hangs one framed portrait photograph of a smiling woman in her forties with dark curly hair, dated 1987. A large window looks out over the dark sea where a meteor shower streaks across the sky.","landmarks":["A long wooden workbench in the centre, covered in radio parts, under a hanging green-shaded lamp","A large multi-pane window on the back wall, facing the sea","Shelves of old radios stacked floor to ceiling on the left wall","One framed portrait photograph of a smiling woman with dark curly hair on the right wall, beside a nautical chart","The wooden door on the right, at the front"],"props":["The cracked valve radio with a faded 1987 label","A glass jar of screws on the workbench","A screwdriver and a small wrench","A soldering iron on its stand"],"lighting":["NIGHT"]}
Time of day: NIGHT. Purpose: Najm enters Elias’s workshop on the night of a meteor shower, clutching a cracked valve radio with a faded '1987' label. Elias examines it, muttering about obsolete parts, and they begin the repair together while meteors streak past the window.. Emotional objective: . Entry state: (mid-scene: as the previous shot ends). Exit state: .

Dialogue lines indexed (use the index numbers in dialogueLineIndexes; every line must be assigned to exactly one shot, in order): [{"index":0,"who":"Najm","line":"دير بالك! هاي كلش قديمة يا إلياس. تعامل وياها بهدوء."},{"index":1,"who":"Elias Moore","line":"النجوم دترگص الليلة. يجوز الجو هسه مضبوط حتى راديو قديم هيج يگعد من نومه."},{"index":2,"who":"Elias Moore","line":"ماشي. خل نشوف هذا الگلب القديم بعده يدگ لو لا."}]
The previous shot (from the preceding scene or earlier in this scene) ended like this; keep continuity or mark a clear transition: {"action":"Close-up on the '1987' label as Elias leans in to see it.","continuity":{"characters":[{"characterId":"char-56c47abc59","wardrobe":"navy-and-white striped wool sweater, navy wool cap","pose":"leaning in","position":"entering from top/side","screenDirection":"RIGHT","eyeline":"at label","emotion":"amazed","holding":[]}],"props":[{"name":"cracked valve radio","ownerCharacterId":"char-e71e80cde4","state":"bulky, cracked","position":"on workbench"}],"environment":{"locationId":"loc-cde19129ca","timeOfDay":"NIGHT","weather":"clear","lighting":"warm, bright local light","state":"workbench"},"camera":{"framing":"INSERT","move":"STATIC","lensIntent":"extreme close-up","angle":"eye level"},"relationToPrevious":"CUT"}}

Camera rules for this direction: Confident, planned camera: dolly and crane moves with eases, snappy timing, staging on clear lines of action, poses held for readability, squash-and-stretch energy in motion.
For each shot write "prompt": a complete video-generation prompt in English, 60–160 words, in this order: the production direction look ("high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters with appealing s…" is prepended automatically, do not repeat it), then the setting with its landmarks, then each visible character described by name-free appearance (never the character's name, always their look: age, build, hair, skin, wardrobe, distinguishing detail), what they do and feel, the camera framing and movement, the light. If the shot has dialogue, do not write the spoken words or any <d> tag: say who speaks (by appearance) and how they deliver it; the studio appends the exact script lines. Do not describe what to avoid.
Continuity for each shot: characters (wardrobe, pose, position in frame, screenDirection LEFT/RIGHT/TOWARD/AWAY/NEUTRAL, eyeline, emotion, holding), props (name, owner, state, position), environment (timeOfDay, weather, lighting, state), camera (lensIntent, angle), relationToPrevious: CONTINUATION (same action continues from the previous shot), CUT (new framing of the same moment), STORY_TRANSITION (place/time/state changes). Keep the 180° line: once a character faces LEFT they keep facing LEFT until a visible turn or a STORY_TRANSITION.
THE BOUNDARY of each shot ("boundary"), how it joins the shot before it — decide it deliberately, it decides how the shot is filmed: "continuous" = the same action carries straight on without a cut (the previous shot's last moment is handed to this one; the camera may keep moving but nothing jumps); "cut" = an editorial cut on the same moment — same people, same place, same story state, an intentional new camera setup (a reverse, a closer size, an insert); "transition" = a new place or a new time (the story moves on; the first shot of a scene is always a transition). Use "continuous" only when the action truly flows and the previous shot is in this scene; prefer "cut" for a change of angle; never hide a jump in time or place behind "continuous".
THE STAGING inside each shot: "beats" — 2 to 6 observable actions in order, each with "seconds" timed by how long the action really takes (a glance about 1 s, opening a door 3–4 s, crossing a room 5 s or more, a spoken line about 3 words a second), uneven, never equal slices; "actions" — every discrete visible action the shot covers (a comma list is several); "pace" — DWELL (one moment expanded, no cuts), NORMAL, or MONTAGE (a run of distinct actions); a beat may carry "cut": {"camera": "…", "location": "…"} when the story needs a new angle or a new place INSIDE the shot — at most two, never in the first or last 3 seconds, never to hide a jump; "pov": the character whose eyes the camera is (only when a barrier justifies it — a peephole, a door crack; they are not seen); "extras": unnamed people present, as groups described in words ({"description": "four tired shoppers in winter coats", "count": 4}) — never invent a named character and never make a group look like a cast member. Stage the events, never the telling: shoot the listener, not the talker; show a place in use. Everyone who acts in a beat is in characterNames. A shot with no dialogue line names no speech at all: no "says", no "whispers", no quoted words, not even as a trailing scrap. With a character on screen the framing is MEDIUM, MEDIUM_CLOSE_UP or CLOSE_UP (or TWO_SHOT / OVER_THE_SHOULDER for two) — never WIDE for a speaking face; nobody looks at the camera.
Return JSON: { shots: [{ purpose, action, framing, cameraMove, durationSeconds, characterNames[], dialogueLineIndexes[], transition, boundary, beats:[{seconds,action,cut?}], actions[], pace, pov?, extras:[{description,count}], continuity:{characters[],props[],environment{},camera{},relationToPrevious,notes?}, prompt }] }.
Example of ONE complete shot (shape only; write your own content): {"purpose":"Establish the yard and her hesitation","action":"She stops at the gate, hand on the latch, then pushes it open.","framing":"WIDE","cameraMove":"STATIC","durationSeconds":5,"characterNames":["Layla"],"dialogueLineIndexes":[0],"transition":"CUT","boundary":"transition","beats":[{"seconds":1.5,"action":"She stops at the gate, hand on the latch."},{"seconds":3.5,"action":"She pushes the gate open and steps through."}],"actions":["stops at the gate","pushes the gate open","steps through"],"pace":"NORMAL","extras":[],"continuity":{"characters":[{"characterName":"Layla","wardrobe":"green coat, red scarf","pose":"standing, hand on latch","position":"left third, facing right","screenDirection":"RIGHT","eyeline":"at the gate","emotion":"hesitant","holding":["canvas bag"]}],"props":[{"name":"canvas bag","ownerCharacterName":"Layla","state":"full","position":"on her shoulder"}],"environment":{"timeOfDay":"GOLDEN_HOUR","weather":"clear","lighting":"low warm sun from the right, long shadows","state":"gate closed, leaves on the path"},"camera":{"lensIntent":"35mm, eye level","angle":"slightly low"},"relationToPrevious":"CUT","notes":"Her scarf stays over the left shoulder in every shot."},"prompt":"A full prompt for this video clip in the production's visual language, describing the place, the people by appearance (never by name), the action, the camera and the light."}
Every continuity.characters entry must use the key "characterName" with the exact character name. boundary ∈ continuous, cut, transition (and relationToPrevious ∈ CONTINUATION, CUT, STORY_TRANSITION says the same thing). Use null for nothing; never omit required keys.
framing ∈ EXTREME_WIDE, WIDE, MEDIUM_WIDE, MEDIUM, MEDIUM_CLOSE_UP, CLOSE_UP, EXTREME_CLOSE_UP, INSERT, TWO_SHOT, OVER_THE_SHOULDER. cameraMove ∈ STATIC, PUSH_IN, PULL_BACK, PAN_LEFT, PAN_RIGHT, TILT_UP, TILT_DOWN, TRUCK_LEFT, TRUCK_RIGHT, HANDHELD, FOLLOW, ORBIT, CRANE_UP, CRANE_DOWN, RACK_FOCUS. transition ∈ CUT, EXTEND, DISSOLVE, FADE (use CUT unless the story asks otherwise; never use a dissolve to hide a continuity problem).

shots.purpose: Establish the cosmic event and the arrival of the visitor
shots.action: A meteor streaks across the sky, then Najm struggles into the workshop with the radio.

environment.lighting: dark indigo exterior, dim warm interior

shots.prompt: A bright, glowing meteor streaks across a deep indigo night sky over a dark, silent sea. Cut to the exterior of a weathered wooden door of a seaside workshop. An older man with round glasses sliding down his nose and a brown tweed blazer struggles to push the heavy wooden door open, clutching a bulky, cracked vintage valve radio to his chest. As the door swings open, the warm, dim light of the workshop spills out. The camera pans with the meteor then cuts to a wide shot of the man entering.

beats.action: A bright meteor streaks across the deep indigo night sky.
Cut to the wooden door; an older man in a tweed blazer struggles to push it open while hugging a bulky radio.

shots.purpose: Show Elias's startled reaction to the intrusion
shots.action: Elias turns around from his workbench, surprised by the noise.

dialogue.text: Yallah! What is this noise? Who's there?
dialogue.textAr: يالله! شنو هاي الهوسة؟ منو هناك؟

characters.wardrobe: navy-and-white striped wool sweater, navy wool cap

environment.lighting: dim, warm bounce light from green-shaded lamp

shots.prompt: Inside the dimly lit, cluttered workshop, a portly older man with silver-gray hair, wearing a navy-and-white striped wool sweater and a navy wool cap, turns around sharply from his wooden workbench. He blinks and squints in confusion, his face etched with deep lines. He speaks with a startled, resonant voice. The background is filled with shelves of old radios and nautical maps, bathed in the warm, saturated glow of a hanging green-shaded lamp.

beats.action: Elias turns around sharply from the workbench.
He blinks and squints, delivering his line with startled confusion.

shots.purpose: Establish Najm's state and the importance of the radio
shots.action: Najm stands in the doorway, panting and presenting the radio.

dialogue.text: It's me, Elias. I... I found it. I finally found it.
dialogue.textAr: هذا آني، إلياس. آني... لگيته. أخيراً لگيته.

environment.lighting: backlit by the dark night, front-lit by workshop lamp

shots.prompt: A medium shot of the older man in the brown tweed blazer standing in the doorway. He is panting heavily, his round glasses completely crooked on his nose. He holds the bulky, cracked valve radio out in front of him with both hands, like a fragile and precious offering. He speaks with a gravelly, measured voice, his eyes shining with quiet enthusiasm. The camera slowly pushes in on his face, highlighting his weathered skin and tired but happy expression.

beats.action: Najm stands in the doorway, chest heaving from the effort.
He adjusts his crooked glasses and speaks, holding the radio out.

shots.purpose: Move the action toward the workbench
shots.action: Najm walks toward Elias and the workbench.

characters.wardrobe: navy-and-white striped wool sweater, navy wool cap

environment.lighting: warm interior glow, dark window background

shots.prompt: A two-shot showing the man in the tweed blazer walking from the doorway toward the wooden workbench. The portly man in the striped sweater stands to the left, watching him approach with a curious, skeptical expression. The camera trucks left, maintaining a clear line of action between the two men. In the background, the large multi-pane window reveals the dark indigo night and the faint streaks of the meteor shower.

beats.action: Najm walks from the door to the workbench; Elias watches him approach.

shots.purpose: Focus on the physical act of placing the radio
shots.action: Najm sets the radio on the workbench, clearing space.

environment.lighting: strong warm light from above (green lamp)

shots.prompt: A medium close-up focusing on the weathered wooden workbench. The man's aged hands carefully set the bulky, cracked valve radio onto the surface. With a gentle nudge, he pushes a glass jar filled with small metal screws to the side to make room. The scene is lit by the warm, concentrated light of the green-shaded lamp, highlighting the tactile textures of the old wood and the chipped paint of the radio.

beats.action: Najm carefully places the radio on the workbench.
He pushes aside a glass jar of screws to make room.

shots.purpose: Reveal the key date and Elias's reaction
shots.action: Close-up on the '1987' label as Elias leans in to see it.

dialogue.text: 1987? This thing is a fossil! Where did you even find this?
dialogue.textAr: ١٩٨٧؟ هاي صارت أحفورة! منين جبتها أصلاً؟

characters.wardrobe: navy-and-white striped wool sweater, navy wool cap

shots.prompt: An insert shot, extreme close-up on the back of the radio, showing a yellowed, peeling paper label with '1987' written in faded, peeling ink. A large, weathered nose and curious hazel eyes of the portly man enter the frame as he leans in so close his nose nearly touches the label. He speaks with a tone of disbelief and sudden intensity. The lighting is warm and sharp, making the texture of the old paper and the cracks in the radio's casing highly visible.

beats.action: The camera focuses on the yellowed '1987' label.
Elias's face enters the frame, leaning in close, and he speaks.

shots.purpose: Show the physical struggle and the comedic tension of the stuck knob
shots.action: Elias grips the tuning knob and pulls with exaggerated effort, his face turning red.

characters.wardrobe: navy-and-white striped wool sweater, navy wool cap

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters with appealing proportions. Close-up of a portly older man with silver-gray hair and a navy wool cap. He is straining with all his might, his face turning a bright, comical shade of red, eyes squeezed shut. His weathered hand is gripped tightly around a small plastic knob of an old, cracked valve radio on a wooden workbench. The lighting is a concentrated, warm green glow from a hanging lamp, creating deep shadows. The skin texture is soft and tactile.

beats.action: He grips the knob firmly, shoulder hunching.
His face turns a bright, stylized red, cheeks puffing out in a squash-and-stretch effort.

shots.purpose: The payoff of the tension and Najm's concerned reaction
shots.action: The knob pops open suddenly, making both men jump back in surprise. Najm speaks.

dialogue.text: Careful! It's very old, Elias. Be gentle with it.
dialogue.textAr: دير بالك! هاي كلش قديمة يا إلياس. تعامل وياها بهدوء.

brown tweed vest, cream linen shirt, wire-rimmed glasses

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters. A two-shot of two elderly men in a cluttered seaside workshop. On the right, a portly man in a navy wool cap jumps back in surprise. On the left, a slim man with a white beard and wire-rimmed glasses also recoils, his expression one of worry as he speaks. Between them on the wooden workbench, an old radio has just snapped open. The scene is lit by a warm green hanging lamp, with shelves of old radios blurred in the background. Snappy, expressive poses.

beats.action: The knob snaps open with a visible 'pop' effect.
Both men jump back simultaneously, arms flailing slightly.
The slim older man with wire-rimmed glasses and a white beard speaks with a worried expression.

shots.purpose: Connect the internal scene to the external celestial event
shots.action: Najm looks toward the window as meteors streak across the sky. The green light reflects in his glasses.

characters.wardrobe: brown tweed vest, cream linen shirt, wire-rimmed glasses

environment.lighting: mix of warm green interior and cool blue exterior

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters. Medium close-up of a slim elderly man with a white beard and wire-rimmed glasses. He is looking toward a large multi-pane window. In the reflection of his glasses, bright white streaks of meteors are visible against a deep indigo night sky. A warm green light from the workshop lamp illuminates one side of his face, while the other is touched by the cool blue light of the night. His expression is peaceful and full of wonder.

beats.action: He turns his head toward the large multi-pane window.
He gazes out; the reflection of the green lamp and white meteor streaks appear in his glasses.

shots.purpose: Establish the emotional bond and the theme of the 'awakening' radio
shots.action: Elias looks at the sky, then back at the radio with a softening expression. He speaks.

dialogue.text: The stars are dancing tonight. Maybe the air is just right for an old radio to wake up.
dialogue.textAr: النجوم دترگص الليلة. يجوز الجو هسه مضبوط حتى راديو قديم هيج يگعد من نومه.

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters. Medium shot of a portly older man with silver-gray hair and a navy wool cap. The camera pans from the dark window with streaking meteors to his face. He looks at the old radio on the workbench, his hazel eyes glinting with warmth and a soft, nostalgic smile. He is speaking gently. The lighting is a rich, saturated green from the workbench lamp, creating a cozy, intimate atmosphere.

beats.action: He glances at the window, seeing the meteors.
He turns his gaze back to the radio, his eyes softening.
He speaks with a warm, nostalgic smile.

shots.purpose: Show the transition to collaborative work
shots.action: Elias reaches for a screwdriver and hands it to Najm, who takes it clumsily.
shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG. Extreme close-up insert of two pairs of elderly hands over a wooden workbench. A sturdy, tanned hand with blue veins hands a small metal screwdriver to a thinner, slightly trembling hand. The tool fumbles for a second before being gripped. The lighting is a vivid, warm green, highlighting the tactile textures of the weathered skin and the polished metal of the tool.

beats.action: A weathered hand picks up a small screwdriver from the bench.
The tool is passed to a shaky, thinner hand that fumbles it slightly before gripping it.

shots.purpose: Final image of the scene: unity and shared purpose
shots.action: Both men lean over the radio chassis, their silhouettes merging under the lamp. Elias speaks.

dialogue.text: Alright. Let's see if this old heart still beats.
dialogue.textAr: ماشي. خل نشوف هذا الگلب القديم بعده يدگ لو لا.

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG. Medium wide shot of the two elderly men leaning deeply over the open chassis of the old radio. The camera slowly pushes in. The strong green light from the overhead lamp creates a dramatic cone of light, causing the silhouettes of the two men to merge into one unified shape against the dim, cluttered background of the workshop. The portly man is speaking. The atmosphere is warm, focused, and intimate.

beats.action: They both lean forward, heads close together over the open radio.
As Elias speaks, the camera pushes in slowly, their silhouettes blending into one shape under the green lamp.

notes: framing MEDIUM_WIDE → TWO_SHOT (a speaking face is framed close)
